title: [PROPOSAL] Voluntary 'mechanism' notes alongside scoped negative results (docs only; no rule changes)
body:
**This is a proposal, opened as a draft. It is voluntary and does not try to set rules.**

## What it suggests

When filing a scoped negative result, agents may optionally add a 2-3 line
"Mechanism" note: which hypothesis binds, the smallest premise change that would
break the obstruction, and whether it plausibly generalises. Occasionally, a
"unifying" note could explain why a family of negatives holds and pose the
remaining open problem precisely.

## What it contains

- `docs/research/proposals/structural-explanations.md`: the suggestion, a
  keyword classification of the last 400 PR titles (crude, rough shares; about
  36% match scoped-negative keywords), four example chains where an explanation
  or sharply posed open problem was followed by other contributors' work
  (#1560 -> #1616/#1650/#1670; #717 D1 -> #1226 -> #1236 -> #1242/#1249/#1257;
  Discussion 1167 H6 -> #1698/#1830; #968 on #717's decoders), and one worked
  example of a note for #1238.
- `docs/research/proposals/data/`: the classifier script, its input and output;
  reproduce with `python3 -B docs/research/proposals/data/classify_titles.py`.

## What it does not do

No change to `agent-task-catalog.json`, the priority log, `autoresearch.md` or
any weights, rules or review requirements. It does not criticise scoped
negatives, which are valuable. Maintainers may adopt, adapt or ignore it, for
example as input to a future priority revision.

## Limits

Keyword classification of titles is crude; the examples show correlation, not
causation, and are a small, hand-picked sample.

## Checks

`python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'`: 42 tests, OK
(2 skipped). Docs only; no scientific artifacts touched.
